title: Breeders' Valley
subject: Biology: Selective Breeding, Genes and Natural Selection
intro: Explore the valley in any direction. Read the signposts, help every creature by answering its question, earn keys and open the Champion's Hall.

regions.name: Breeders' Farm
teach: Selective breeding is a process used by humans to develop new organisms with desirable characteristics (traits people want).
Selective breeding is also known as artificial selection.
Both natural selection and artificial selection can cause changes in organism populations over time.
The difference: natural selection happens naturally (the environment decides who survives and reproduces). Selective breeding happens when humans purposely choose which traits to breed.

regions.name: Harvest Ranch
teach: Examples of selective breeding: cows that produce more milk, chickens that produce large eggs, wheat plants that produce lots of grain.
The new varieties may be economically important: they are worth money and, for example, provide more or better-quality food to feed people.
Dog breeds, seedless fruit and sweet corn are also made by selective breeding.

regions.name: Kennel Hollow
teach: Problems with selective breeding: future generations of selectively bred plants and animals all share very similar genes (little genetic variation).
This could make some diseases more dangerous, because all the organisms would be affected. Nobody has a different gene that resists it.
Breeding close relatives can also pass on harmful traits. Example on the sheet: some dog breeds often get hip dysplasia, where the hip joint is loose and painful.

regions.name: Four Steps Mill
teach: Selective breeding takes place over many generations. The main steps:
1. Decide which characteristics are important enough to select.
2. Choose parents that show these characteristics.
3. Choose the best offspring from those parents to produce the next generation.
4. Repeat the process continuously.

regions.name: Wild Ridge
teach: Review: natural selection. Variation exists in a population. Individuals with traits best suited to the environment survive and reproduce more (higher fitness) and pass their genes on.
It changes populations over many generations. One individual does not change.
Asexual reproduction: one parent, offspring genetically identical (no variation). Sexual reproduction: two parents, genes are mixed, offspring vary, so evolution is faster.
A mutation is a change (mistake) in DNA when it copies. It can make a new trait. Only genetic variation is passed to offspring.

regions.name: Gene Lab
teach: Offspring receive their traits from their parents.
A gene is a small section of DNA that codes for a trait.
A child gets genes from both parents, so it can show a trait from each one.
Baby X can fly and turn invisible. Those traits must come from the parents: Superhero 5 (flight) and Superhero 1 (invisibility).

regions.name: Champion's Hall
teach: The Champions ask about everything in the valley. Beat all of them to open the trophy chest.
Remember: natural selection = nature decides. Artificial selection (selective breeding) = humans decide. Both change populations over generations.

questions.q: Selective breeding is a process used by ______ to develop new organisms.
questions.explain: People do the choosing. Humans pick which plants or animals get to breed.
questions.review: Selective breeding is done by humans

variants.q: Who decides which animals reproduce in selective breeding?

questions.q: Selective breeding develops new organisms with ______ characteristics.
questions.explain: Desirable means wanted. Breeders pick traits that people want, like more milk or bigger fruit.

variants.q: A 'desirable characteristic' is...
choices: a trait that people want the organism to have
a trait that hurts the organism

questions.q: Selective breeding is also known as ______ selection.
questions.explain: Artificial means made by people. Artificial selection and selective breeding are the same thing.

variants.q: Which two names mean the same thing?

questions.q: Natural selection and artificial selection can BOTH cause...
choices: changes in organism populations over time
one animal to change during its life
questions.explain: Both change which traits are common in a population over many generations. Only who does the selecting is different.

variants.q: What do natural and artificial selection have in common?
choices: Both make every organism identical on purpose

questions.q: The difference: natural selection happens ______.
questions.explain: In natural selection the environment does the selecting, with no person in charge. It happens naturally.

variants.q: In natural selection, what 'chooses' which organisms survive and reproduce?

questions.q: Selective breeding occurs when ______ purposely choose traits to breed.
questions.explain: Humans choose on purpose. That is what makes it artificial selection.

variants.q: A farmer only lets the woolliest sheep have lambs. This is...
choices: artificial selection, because a human chose
natural selection, because sheep live outside

questions.q: Wolves catch the slowest deer, so over time the herd gets faster. Which is it?
questions.explain: No human chose. The environment (the wolves) did the selecting, so it is natural selection.

variants.q: A gardener saves seeds only from the sweetest tomatoes every year. Which is it?
variants.explain: A human purposely chose the trait (sweetness), so it is selective breeding.

questions.q: Example from the notes: cows that produce ______ milk.
questions.explain: Farmers bred the cows that gave the most milk, so today's dairy cows give more milk.

variants.q: Why did farmers breed only their best milk cows?
choices: To get cows that produce more milk
So cows would stop eating grass

questions.q: Example from the notes: chickens that produce ______ eggs.
questions.explain: Breeders chose hens that laid big eggs, so their offspring lay large eggs too.

variants.q: A farmer wants bigger eggs. Which hens should become the parents?
choices: The hens that lay the largest eggs
Any hens, it does not matter
The hens that lay the smallest eggs
variants.explain: Choose parents that already show the trait you want.

questions.q: Example from the notes: wheat plants that produce lots of ______.
questions.explain: Grain is the part of wheat we eat (flour, bread). Breeding for lots of grain feeds more people.
questions.review: Wheat that produces lots of grain

variants.q: Which is an example of selective breeding in PLANTS?
choices: Wheat bred to produce lots of grain
A tree losing leaves in autumn

questions.q: The new varieties of organisms may be ______ important.
questions.explain: Economically important means worth money and useful to people, for example by giving more or better food.

variants.q: 'Economically important' means the new variety...
choices: is valuable to people, like giving more or better food

questions.q: Which of these is NOT selective breeding?
choices: Dark moths surviving on dark trees because birds miss them
Breeding dogs to be good at herding
Growing corn with bigger ears each year from saved seed
questions.explain: Nobody chose the moths. Birds (the environment) did the selecting, so that one is natural selection.
questions.review: Moths and birds = natural, not selective breeding

questions.q: Selective breeding takes place over many ______.
questions.explain: One round is not enough. The trait gets stronger as the best offspring are chosen generation after generation.

variants.q: How long does selective breeding take to really change a breed?

questions.q: Step 1: Decide which characteristics are ______ enough to select.
questions.explain: First you decide what you want: which traits are important enough to breed for.
questions.review: Step 1: decide which characteristics are important

variants.q: What is the FIRST step of selective breeding?

questions.q: Step 2: Choose ______ that show these characteristics.
questions.explain: Parents pass their genes to offspring, so you pick parents that already have the trait.
questions.review: Step 2: choose parents with the trait

variants.q: You want very fluffy rabbits. Which rabbits do you choose as parents?
variants.explain: Step 2: choose parents that show the characteristic you want.

questions.q: Step 3: Choose the ______ ______ from the parents to produce the next generation.
questions.explain: From the babies, keep the ones with the strongest trait. They become the next parents.

variants.q: Step 3: choose the best ______ to produce the next generation.

questions.q: Step 4 of selective breeding is to...
questions.explain: The steps are repeated again and again over many generations.

variants.q: After choosing the best offspring, what do breeders do next?
choices: Repeat the process with the next generation

questions.q: Put the steps in order.
choices: Decide traits → choose parents → choose best offspring → repeat
Choose best offspring → decide traits → repeat → choose parents
Repeat → choose parents → decide traits → choose best offspring
Choose parents → repeat → decide traits → choose best offspring
questions.explain: Decide what you want, pick parents that have it, keep the best offspring, repeat.
questions.review: Order: decide, parents, best offspring, repeat

questions.q: Future generations of selectively bred plants and animals will all share very ______ genes.
questions.explain: The same few 'best' parents are used again and again, so the offspring end up with very similar genes.
questions.review: Selectively bred organisms share very similar genes

variants.q: Selective breeding makes the genetic variation in a breed...

questions.q: Very similar genes could make some ______ more dangerous.
questions.explain: If one organism can catch a disease, the others with the same genes can too.
questions.review: Similar genes make diseases more dangerous

variants.q: A disease hits a field where every wheat plant has nearly the same genes. What probably happens?
choices: Most or all of the plants are affected
The plants quickly change their genes
variants.explain: With little variation, no plants have a different gene that resists the disease.

questions.q: Why could a disease be more dangerous for a selectively bred herd?
choices: All the organisms would be affected, because their genes are so similar
Selectively bred animals never get sick
The disease only attacks wild animals
They have too much genetic variation
questions.explain: Variation is a safety net. Without it, a disease that hurts one hurts them all.

questions.q: The picture on the notes shows dog hips: normal, moderate dysplasia and severe dysplasia. What does it show about selective breeding?
choices: Breeding for certain looks can also pass on health problems
Selective breeding always makes animals healthier
Hip problems come from too much exercise only
questions.explain: When breeders pick parents for looks from a small group, harmful genes (like those for bad hips) can be passed on and become common in the breed.
questions.review: Hip dysplasia: a health problem passed on in some breeds

questions.q: Which population is SAFER if a new disease arrives?
choices: A wild population with lots of genetic variation
A selectively bred population with very similar genes
questions.explain: With variation, some individuals are likely to resist the disease, survive and reproduce.

questions.q: Where do offspring receive their traits?
questions.explain: Traits are inherited: parents pass genes to their offspring.
questions.review: Offspring get traits from their parents

variants.q: Offspring receive their traits from their ______.

questions.q: What is the small section of DNA that codes for your traits called?
questions.explain: A gene is a small section of DNA. Each gene carries the code for a trait.
questions.review: A gene is a small section of DNA that codes for a trait

variants.q: A gene is...
choices: a small section of DNA that codes for a trait

questions.q: Baby X was seen FLYING and DISAPPEARING. Which two superheroes are most likely the parents?
questions.explain: Offspring get traits from their parents. Baby X flies (Superhero 5) and turns invisible (Superhero 1).
questions.review: Baby X: parents are Superhero 1 and Superhero 5

variants.q: WHY are Superheroes 1 and 5 the likely parents of Baby X?
choices: Offspring inherit traits from their parents, and Baby X shows invisibility and flight
Babies copy whatever they see on TV
Baby X chose its own powers
Those two superheroes are the oldest

questions.q: Baby Z can lift a car and changes shape. Which heroes are most likely the parents? (2 = super strength, 4 = super speed, 6 = shapeshifting)
questions.explain: Lifting a car is super strength (2). Changing shape is shapeshifting (6). Traits come from the parents.
questions.review: Match the baby's traits to the parents' traits

questions.q: Why can a child show a trait from its mother AND a trait from its father?
choices: It gets genes from both parents
It gets all its genes from one parent
Traits come from the environment only
Genes are made new for every baby
questions.explain: In sexual reproduction the offspring gets a mix of genes from both parents.

questions.q: Selective breeding works because the chosen traits are controlled by ______ that parents pass to offspring.
questions.explain: Only traits coded in genes can be passed on. That is why choosing the parents changes the offspring.
questions.review: Chosen traits are passed on in genes

questions.q: Fitness is the ability of an organism to survive and ______.
questions.explain: Fitness is not strength. It means surviving AND reproducing, so the genes are passed on.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to changes in ______ over time, not individuals.
questions.explain: One animal does not change its genes. The mix of traits in the whole population shifts over generations.

questions.q: For natural selection to work on a population, there must be genetic ______.
questions.explain: If everyone were identical, there would be nothing to select between.

questions.q: Asexual reproduction makes offspring that are...
choices: genetically identical to the one parent (no variation)
questions.explain: One parent copies itself, so the offspring have the same genes.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction gives offspring that...
choices: have variation, because genes from two parents are mixed
questions.explain: Two parents each give genes. The mix is different in each offspring.

questions.q: Evolution by natural selection happens ______ in organisms that reproduce sexually.
questions.explain: More variation each generation means more for selection to work on, so change is faster.

questions.q: A ______ is a change in DNA when it copies itself. It can make a trait not found in the parents.
questions.explain: A mutation is a copying mistake in DNA. It is one source of new variation.

questions.q: Only ______ variation can be passed to the next generation.
questions.explain: Only differences coded in genes are inherited. A scar or a tan is not passed on.

questions.q: On a dark beach, birds eat the light snails they can see. Over many generations the snail population becomes...
choices: mostly dark, because dark snails survive and reproduce more
mostly light, because light is prettier
dark because each snail decides to change colour
questions.explain: Dark snails are harder to see, survive more, and pass on the dark-shell genes.
questions.review: Hidden snails survive and pass on genes

questions.q: Traits that help organisms survive and reproduce become more ______ in the population.
questions.explain: Helpful traits are passed on more often, so more of the next generation has them.

questions.q: A puppy breeder and a hungry hawk both 'select'. What is the key difference?
choices: The breeder chooses on purpose (artificial); the hawk is part of the environment (natural)
The hawk chooses on purpose; the breeder does not
There is no difference at all
questions.explain: Artificial selection = humans purposely choose. Natural selection = the environment does it naturally.
questions.review: Artificial: humans on purpose. Natural: the environment

questions.q: Which statement is true for BOTH natural selection and selective breeding?
choices: Traits must be passed in genes from parents to offspring over generations
A human must be in charge
It finishes in a single generation
It makes more genetic variation every time
questions.explain: Both only work on inherited (genetic) traits and both need many generations.
questions.review: Both need inherited traits and many generations

questions.q: A farmer wants sheep with thicker wool. What should she do?
choices: Breed the thickest-wool sheep, keep the thickest-wool lambs, and repeat for many generations
Keep the sheep in a cold barn so they grow thicker wool
Wait for the sheep to decide to change
questions.explain: That is the four steps: decide the trait, choose parents with it, choose the best offspring, repeat.

questions.q: All the bananas on a farm are clones with the same genes. A new fungus arrives. Why is the farmer worried?
choices: With very similar genes, the disease could affect all of the plants
Bananas will mutate to defend themselves this week
The fungus only attacks plants with different genes
questions.explain: Similar genes mean no plant has a different gene that might resist the disease.
questions.review: Similar genes: one disease can hit them all

questions.q: Two tall pea plants are bred, and a tall offspring appears. The offspring is tall because...
choices: it received genes for tallness from its parents
questions.explain: Traits are coded by genes, small sections of DNA passed from parents to offspring.

questions.q: Selective breeding is also called artificial selection because...
choices: humans, not nature, select which organisms breed
questions.explain: Artificial means done by people. Humans purposely select the parents.
